```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
options(width = 750)
library(orthologr)
# TRUE if DIAMOND2 is on the PATH or was installed with diamond_install()
has_diamond <- tryCatch({ diamond_path(); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  comment = "#>",
  collapse = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  tidy = FALSE,
  eval = has_diamond)
```

`orthologr` infers orthologous genes between genomes, estimates their dN/dS, and
clusters proteins into homologous groups, all without leaving the R environment.
Four steps get you started.

## 1. Install `orthologr`

```{r,eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("Biostrings", "GenomicRanges", "GenomicFeatures",
                       "Rsamtools", "rtracklayer", "pwalign"))
install.packages(c("doParallel", "foreach", "ape", "Rdpack", "benchmarkme", "devtools"))
devtools::install_github("drostlab/metablastr")
devtools::install_github("drostlab/orthologr")
```

Windows users also need [Rtools](setup_windows.html#install-rtools).

## 2. Install DIAMOND2

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(orthologr)
diamond_install()
```

This downloads `DIAMOND2` for your operating system into a user cache folder, with no
administrator rights or `PATH` changes. It is the only external tool needed for steps 3 and 4.
See [Install](Install.html#diamond-install) for alternatives (conda, manual install, BLAST+).

## 3. Estimate dN/dS with `dNdS()`

`dNdS()` finds orthologous gene pairs between two species and computes dN, dS and dN/dS for each pair
from their coding sequences.

```{r}
dnds <- dNdS(
  query_file     = system.file("seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta", package = "orthologr"),
  subject_file   = system.file("seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta", package = "orthologr"),
  print_citation = FALSE
)

head(dnds[, c("query_id", "subject_id", "dN", "dS", "dNdS")])
```

More: [Orthology inference](orthology_inference.html), [dNdS estimation](dNdS_estimation.html),
[Divergence stratigraphy](divergence_stratigraphy.html).

## 4. Cluster proteins with `deepclust()`

`deepclust()` groups the proteins of one or more proteomes into homologous clusters.

```{r}
clusters <- deepclust(
  input_file = c(
    system.file("seqs/ortho_thal_aa.fasta", package = "orthologr"),
    system.file("seqs/ortho_lyra_aa.fasta", package = "orthologr")
  ),
  mutual_cover = 70 # 70% mutual coverage of the aligned sequences
)

head(clusters)
```

More: [Protein clustering with DeepClust](deepclust.html).
